text: In 1977, a telescope picked up a signal from space so strong, the astronomer could only write one word.
He circled it on the printout, and wrote: Wow!
It came from the direction of Sagittarius, and it lasted seventy-two seconds.
That's exactly how long the Big Ear telescope could watch one spot, as the Earth turned.
And it sat right by the radio frequency of hydrogen. The one many scientists thought aliens would use.
So they pointed telescopes back at that spot. Again, and again, for decades.
In 2024, a team studying old data from the Arecibo telescope suggested an answer.
A cold cloud of hydrogen, suddenly lit up by a blast from something like a magnetar, a dead star with a monstrous magnetic field.
It's not proven yet. So for now, the most famous signal ever recorded is still just one word.
